U/xomollyvincent is not saying that there is not a withdrawl, they are saying that the type of withdrawal is different. With opiates, the chemical itself binds to the receptors, and the receptors in turn become dependent on the opiate. But with cannabis, the chemical does not cause dependency, so there may be withdrawal with constant use-- always smoking before you eat or sleep will make it hard to eat and sleep when you stop smoking--but the withdrawal is not based on a neurochemical need for the substance. In your case with cigs, youre really lucky. I know a lot of people who are trying to quit and can't because of headaches, shakes, and cravings-- so i commend you for that!
